newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak energy prices to rise 10 pct for companies.
newsitem.headline: Slovak energy prices to rise 10 pct for companies.

text.p: The Slovak government on Tuesday approved an average 10 percent increase in energy prices for corporate consumers, effective August 1, 1997.
However the government rejected a proposal for a 20 percent energy price hike for private consumers, Economics Minister Karol Cesnek told a news conference during a regular government session.

"The government approved only a part of a price increase package, that for corporate customers, and ordered our ministry to submit a detailed analysis of possible impacts of energy price increases for private consumers," Cesnek said.
He said the price hike was expected to boost producer prices by an average "two to three percentage points."
The Slovak producer price index (PPI) rose 0.2 percent, month-on-month, in June, putting prices 3.7 percent higher than in the same month of the previous year.

Cesnek would not comment on the possible impact of the energy price hike on consumer prices, but last Friday Finance Minister Sergej Kozlik said a series of planned hikes in regulated prices would boost the Consumer Price Index (CPI) by one percentage point later this year.
Apart from the energy price increase for corporate customers, the most significant hike should be a 10 percent increase in heating prices for citizens expected to come into effect from next month.
Consumer prices rose by 0.3 percent month-on-month in June 1997 after a 0.1 percent monthly increase in May.
Annual inflation was 6.2 percent in June 1997, compared with a 6.1 percent year-on-year increase in May.
